When Mendel published his results in 1866, the scientific world largely ignored them. His paper was cited only a handful of times in the next 35 years. It was not until 1900 — 16 years after Mendel's death — that three botanists independently rediscovered his laws and finally found his original paper, launching the science of genetics.
